sections.html:
Pueblo stands where Fountain Creek meets the Arkansas River, about 112 miles south of Denver, and it is the seat of Pueblo County. The 2020 census counted 111,876 people, which made it the ninth largest city in Colorado. Interstate 25 is the quick route north to Colorado Springs and Denver, so a buyer pricing your house often has Colorado Springs or Canon City listings open in another tab.

The city was assembled from four towns: Pueblo, South Pueblo, Central Pueblo and Bessemer. Bessemer, the steelworker neighborhood on the south side, joined last, in 1894. Street patterns, lot sizes and house styles change fast from one part of town to the next, so an appraiser or buyer will look hard at the blocks around your address and care little about a citywide average.

Steel shaped Pueblo's housing. Colorado Fuel and Iron ran the south side mill for close to a century and was the biggest employer in the state. Families arrived from Ireland, Italy, Germany, Slovenia, Greece and elsewhere, and many of the blocks they settled still have homes from the mill's early decades. The mill continues today as Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel with far fewer workers.

The Great Flood of 1921 is the other event people remember, and it cost the city roughly one-third of its downtown businesses. That history is why buyers of older houses near the river or a creek ask about drainage and basement moisture. If you own one, pull together whatever you have: repair receipts, notes on past water, anything about a sump pump.

sections.h2: How sun and temperature swings wear on a house
sections.html:
Pueblo gets only about 12 inches of precipitation a year but nearly 3,470 hours of sunshine. Summer highs reach 90 degrees or more on about 72 days, and the daily swing between the high and the low averages about 32.5 degrees. Shingles, exterior paint, window seals and concrete all take a beating from that combination.

If a roof or paint job has been put off, expect a cash buyer to price the work into the offer instead of asking you to do it. A buyer who finances may ask for repairs before the loan can close.

sections.h2: Code enforcement notices on a vacant or inherited house
sections.html:
Pueblo's Code Enforcement team deals with litter, weeds, parking, inoperable vehicles stored on a lot, and graffiti. A person who receives a notice and has not complied after 10 days can be summoned to municipal court.

Vacant and inherited properties pick up notices easily, since nobody is mowing or hauling away a junk car while the family decides what to do. Open the notice the day it arrives, and either fix the problem or tell the buyer about it early. If the city's community service program removes graffiti from private property, the owner signs a release of liability first.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Pueblo County
sections.html:
ChargeAmountApplies to
Pueblo County recording feeFlat $43Each real estate document, since July 1, 2025
State documentary fee, C.R.S. 39-13-102$0.01 per $100Any document conveying real property; none at $500 or less

The county's flat fee took effect after Colorado HB 24-1269. Your title company handles both charges at closing. For questions, the Pueblo County recording phone line is 719-583-6507, and the fee schedule is on the Pueblo County Clerk and Recorder's page.

sections.h2: Which school district is my Pueblo house in?
sections.html: Nearly the whole city is inside Pueblo School District 60, and very small pieces fall in Pueblo County School District 70. A house near the city edge is the one case worth checking, so use the district's address lookup before telling a buyer.

Black Hills Energy is the electric company in Pueblo. Schedule a final meter reading and move service out of your name on the closing date, so the bills stop when the keys change hands. Take a photo of each meter on moving day, because a dated picture settles any later argument about the last reading.

Pueblo is also a city where friends and relatives of an heir often live out of town. If that describes you, let the title company know early so documents can be signed by mail or in front of a notary where you live.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like for a Pueblo homeowner
sections.html:
With a cash buyer there is no mortgage underwriting and no lender appraisal, which removes the two steps that most often delay a closing. You describe the house, the buyer looks it over, and you accept an offer or you do not.

  • No repairs or cleaning are expected beforehand.
  • The closing date can follow your moving plans.
  • A title company still prepares the deed and records it with the county.
  • You can set the offer next to a listing with an agent before choosing.

Pueblo owners usually reach us in one of four situations: an inherited house, tenants who left damage, a vacant property that has drawn code notices, or a mortgage that has fallen behind.

If you are weighing the offer, think through the order of events. First comes the walkthrough and the written offer. Then the title company opens a file, confirms who owns the property and finds any payoff owed to a lender. Last, you sign the deed, the fees listed above are paid, and the deed is recorded. Having your loan servicer's contact information and any open code notices in one folder keeps each step moving.

A sale also ends your responsibility for the property. Once the deed is recorded, the yard, the roof and the code notices belong to the new owner, which is a relief for anyone who has been managing a house from a distance.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you talk to a buyer
sections.html:
Pueblo sellers move faster when the file is ready. Put these items in one place before the first call:

  • The deed or any probate paperwork, if the house came to you through an estate.
  • The latest mortgage statement, or the servicer's phone number if you are behind.
  • Every code notice the city has sent, along with proof of anything you already fixed.
  • Leases and a tenant contact, when someone is still living there.
  • Notes on the roof, the furnace and any water in the basement.

Nothing on that list has to be perfect. A buyer who purchases as is expects some gaps, and the title company fills in the rest. What slows a sale is not knowing where a document is, so even a rough folder helps.

faqs.q: How many people live in Pueblo, Colorado?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 111,876 residents, which made Pueblo the ninth largest city in Colorado. The most recent estimate, from July 1, 2025, is 110,404.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Pueblo house if it has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can take a house with open notices for litter, weeds or inoperable vehicles. The city allows 10 days to comply before a municipal court summons, so address any notice or raise it with the buyer early.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Pueblo County?
faqs.a: Pueblo County charges a flat $43 per real estate document, effective July 1, 2025. The state documentary fee is $0.01 per $100, with none owed at $500 or less. The title company usually collects both.

faqs.q: Does Pueblo's climate affect what a buyer will offer?
faqs.a: It can. Heavy sun and big temperature swings wear roofs, paint and windows. A cash buyer will price those repairs into the offer instead of asking you to fix them.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Pueblo house in?
faqs.a: Almost all of the city is in Pueblo School District 60, and very small portions are in District 70. Check the district's address lookup if you live near the city edge.
